title: Myerson Optimal Auction (Virtual Valuations)
body_html:
Myerson Optimal Auction (Virtual Valuations)

Theorem (Myerson 1981; MSZ Thm 12.26). For a regular IPV selling problem ([[mechanism_design.bayesian.selling_problem]]) — meaning each bidder $i$'s virtual valuation $$ \psi_i(t_i) \;=\; t_i \;-\; \frac{1 - F_i(t_i)}{f_i(t_i)} $$ is non-decreasing in $t_i$ — the expected-revenue-maximising BIC selling mechanism is:

  1. Allocate the object to the bidder $i^* = \arg\max_i \psi_i(t_i)$ provided $\psi_{i^*}(t_{i^*}) \ge 0$; otherwise leave the object unsold.
  2. Charge the winner their threshold bid: the smallest type that would have won given the others' reports.

Why virtual valuations

Combining revenue equivalence ([[mechanism_design.myerson.revenue_equivalence]]) with the Myerson payment formula ([[mechanism_design.myerson.payment_formula]]) shows that expected revenue equals expected virtual welfare: $$ \mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_i \psi_i(t_i) \cdot x_i(t)\Big]. $$ Subject to monotonicity of $x_i(\cdot, t_{-i})$ in own type (required for incentive compatibility), this expectation is point-wise maximised by allocating to the bidder with highest non-negative virtual valuation. Regularity ($\psi_i$ monotone) ensures the resulting allocation rule is itself monotone, satisfying the BIC constraint automatically.

When some $\psi_i$ is not monotone (non-regular case), the optimal solution uses ironing: replace $\psi_i$ on intervals where it would decrease with a constant value chosen to preserve the integral. Ironing is non-trivial to formalise but the regular case is the headline result.

Specialisation

In the symmetric IPV setting (all $F_i = F$, all $v_i$ identical), the optimal auction is a second-price auction with reserve price $r^* = \psi^{-1}(0)$ — see [[mechanism_design.myerson.reserve_price]].

Lean port (deferred — see #175)

Planned new module: EconCSLib/MechanismDesign/MyersonOptimalAuction.lean.

Planned declarations:

  • virtualValuation (def)
  • IsRegular (monotone virtual valuations)
  • myersonOptimalAuction (the mechanism)
  • myersonOptimalAuction_isBIC (incentive compatibility)
  • myersonOptimalAuction_maximises_expectedRevenue (main theorem)

Ironing for non-regular distributions is a separate, more delicate task (distinguished kind: proof-plan follow-up).

This is the most mathematically dense item in the MSZ Ch.12 cluster; research-level Lean port expected.

References

  • [MSZ Thm 12.26] Maschler, Solan, Zamir, Game Theory, references/GameTheory.pdf.
  • Myerson, R. B. (1981). "Optimal Auction Design". Math. Oper. Res. 6: 58–73.
  • Krishna, V. (2010). Auction Theory, Ch. 5. references/AuctionTheory.pdf.
